description: lower braking_factor 3.5->2.0: no change (tow_truck bottleneck is not curvature-braking-gated -- car_base/trailer_truck got faster but aggregate (=tow_truck) unchanged)

diagnosed tow_truck bottleneck via debug telemetry: it gets permanently wedged (0 velocity even under full reverse -- a rigid physical lock, not just drag) at a specific tight corner because it arrives too fast/late-braking; brake earlier+harder for corners (curvature_preview 12->25, braking_factor 3.5->6.0, min_speed 4->2.5, safety_margin 1.1->0.8), stop braking on climbs (only descents -- braking on a climb only bleeds momentum needed to crest it), add generic stuck-detection+reverse-recovery maneuver. tow_truck avoids the first jam and gets much further before falling off elsewhere, but the much harder braking makes car_base/trailer_truck no longer finish in time (mean 0.886 -> 0.665): 0.275558 -> 0.281397

ease off the previous experiment's corner braking (curvature_preview 25->18, braking_factor 6.0->4.5, min_speed 2.5->3.0, safety_margin 0.8->0.9): car_base now finishes the whole track again (score 1.128, reason=won), trailer_truck gets much further before falling (0.806), tow_truck still bottleneck but improved too (0.309, no longer falls off, just times out). Both aggregate and mean up: 0.281397 -> 0.308798, mean 0.664994 -> 0.747599

lower cross_track_gain 0.75->0.5: less aggressive centerline-correction pull, hypothesized to reduce trailer sway feeding into tow_truck's tight-corner jam. tow_truck reaches further (113m->125m) before running out of time, others roughly unchanged (car_base still wins, trailer still falls off around the same spot): 0.308798 -> 0.340507

lower cross_track_gain further 0.5->0.3: worse, not better -- with even less correction the car now drifts enough that car_base ALSO falls off (previously it won cleanly), and tow_truck fell off instead of just timing out. Too little cross-track correction lets lateral drift compound. 0.340507 -> 0.289661 (reverted)

react to being stuck faster and reverse longer (stuck_time_threshold 1.5->0.8, recovery_reverse_time 1.2->2.0): worse -- tow_truck now falls off earlier (102m) instead of just timing out further along (125m); the longer/earlier reverse apparently backs it into trouble rather than freeing it. 0.340507 -> 0.279074 (reverted)
